translations.text: And the word of the Lord came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying:
“Get up and go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach there, for the outcry of its wickedness has reached me.”

And Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. He paid the fare and boarded it to sail with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the Lord.
And the Lord stirred up a wind on the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship was in danger of breaking apart.

And the sailors were greatly afraid, and each cried out to his own gods. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten their load. But Jonah had gone down into a recess of the ship and was sleeping and snoring.
The captain approached him and said, “Why are you snoring like this? Get up and call upon the Lord your God. Perhaps God will save us, and we will not perish.”
And they said to one another, “Come, let us cast lots and find out on whose account these troubles have come upon us.” They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

And they said to him, “Tell us why these troubles have come upon us. What is your occupation? Where do you come from, or where are you going? What country are you from, and what people do you belong to?”
He said to them, “I am a servant of the Lord, and I worship the Lord, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
And the men were greatly afraid and said to him, “What have you done?” For they knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the Lord, because he had told them.
And they said to him, “What shall we do to you so that the sea will grow calm for us?” For the sea was growing still more turbulent and raising a storm against them.
And Jonah said to them, “Pick me up and throw me into the sea, and the sea will grow calm for you, for I know that this great storm has come upon you because of me.”
And the men tried hard to bring the ship back to dry land, but they could not, for the sea grew more and more turbulent and fierce against them.
They cried out to the Lord and said, “Let it not be, Lord! Do not let us perish because of this man’s life, and do not hold us guilty of innocent blood, for you, Lord, have done as you wished.”
And they picked up Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea ceased its raging.
And the men feared the Lord greatly, offered sacrifices to the Lord, and made vows.
And the Lord commanded a great sea creature to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the sea creature for three days and three nights.
And Jonah prayed to the Lord God from the belly of the sea creature,
and said, “In my distress I cried out to the Lord my God, and he heard me. From the belly of the underworld I cried out; Lord, hear my voice.
You cast me into the depths of the heart of the sea, and rivers surrounded me. All your surges and your waves passed over me.
And I said, ‘I have been driven away from your sight. Will I now look again upon your holy temple?’
The waters poured over me, reaching my soul; unfathomable depths surrounded me. My head went into the clefts of the mountains.
I went down to the earth, whose bars are [?] forever. May my life rise out of corruption
to you, Lord my God. When my soul was fainting, I called upon the Lord and remembered him, and may my prayers come into your holy temple.
Those who clung to vanity and falsehood abandoned their own mercy.
But I will offer you a sacrifice with a voice of praise and thanksgiving, and I will pay what I have vowed to the Lord for salvation.
And the Lord commanded the monstrous fish, and it vomited him onto dry land.
And the word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, saying:
Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim in it the first proclamation that I spoke to you.
Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, as the Lord had told him. Now Nineveh was a great city before God, about a three days’ journey across.
Jonah began to enter the city, going about a day’s journey, and proclaimed, saying, “Three more days, and Nineveh will be overthrown.”
The people of Nineveh believed in God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from their greatest to their least.
The word reached the king of Nineveh. He arose from his throne, took off his robe, put on sackcloth, and sat on ashes.
A proclamation was announced in Nineveh by the king and his nobles: “Let neither humans nor animals, flocks nor cattle, taste anything. Let them neither graze nor drink water.”
Humans and animals put on sackcloth, and they cried out to God wholeheartedly. Each turned from their own evil ways and from the lawlessness in their hands.
And they said, “Who knows? God may relent and turn from his fierce anger, so that we do not perish.”
God saw their deeds, that each had turned from their own evil ways. God relented concerning the calamity he had said he would bring upon them, and he did not bring it.
Jonah was deeply distressed and troubled.

He prayed to the Lord God and said, “O Lord, is this not what I said while I was still in my own country? That is why I hurried to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that you are merciful and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in mercy, and that you relent concerning calamity.”
“And now, Lord, Lord, take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to remain alive.”
The Lord said to Jonah, “Are you truly so deeply distressed?”
Jonah went out of the city and sat facing the city. He made himself a shelter and sat beneath its shade until he could see what would happen to the city.
God commanded a gourd plant, and it grew up over Jonah’s head to provide shade over his head and relieve him of his suffering. Jonah rejoiced greatly over the gourd plant.
God commanded a worm early the next morning, and it struck the gourd plant, so that it withered.

When the sun rose, God commanded a scorching, burning wind. The sun beat down on Jonah’s head, and he was in distress, and his life was ebbing away. He said, “It would be better for me to die than to live this life.”
The Lord God said to Jonah, “Are you truly so deeply distressed over the gourd plant?” He said, “I am deeply distressed, even to the point of death.”
The Lord said, “You had pity on the gourd plant, for which you did not labor and which you did not nurture. It grew in one night and perished the next night.”
Should I not spare Nineveh, the great city, in which live more than 120,000 people who do not know their right hand from their left, and many animals?
